title: Generation Is Cheap, Review Is Expensive: How to Stop Shipping AI Slop — Gabriel Martinez, G2i
talk_summary: Gabriel Martinez argues that AI generation is cheap but human evaluation is the real bottleneck, so slop arises when generation outruns judgment. He prescribes reducing decision surface via conventions, small reviewable PRs, diagrams as compressed review surfaces, and accountability metrics tied to value rather than token/PR volume.

takeaways.technique: Cap PR size to keep review surface human-reviewable
takeaways.what_they_do: Decompose needs into smallest chunks so each change is small enough to hold in your head and actually review; treat multi-thousand-line PRs as unreviewable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: There's no way in hell that a human can fully understand all the important bits of a change that big.

takeaways.technique: Convention-over-configuration to shrink agent decision surface
takeaways.what_they_do: Enforce one canonical way to structure each concept so agents don't produce five plausible patterns in five styles that reviewers must reverse-engineer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: An agent can generate five plausible patterns in five different styles. And now the human reviewer has to reverse engineer not just the code but the intent behind it

takeaways.technique: Reject artifact expansion; require ambiguity resolved by the doer
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat a vague 10-bullet scope returned as a 20-page doc as failure: the output expanded the problem instead of clarifying it, pushing work onto reviewers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It took ambiguity that should have been resolved by the person doing the work and handed it back as a larger artifact

takeaways.technique: Diagrams and declarative layers as compressed review surface
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the main workflow as the reviewable surface with implementation pushed to leaves; use diagrams of boundaries, data flows, state transitions, failure modes instead of reading all code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: humans need a compressed review surface. service boundaries, data flows, state transitions, and failure modes

takeaways.technique: Accountability metrics tied to value, not output volume
takeaways.what_they_do: Make per-chunk accountability visible so engineers/agents are incentivized to be meticulous; reward elegant design and clear test harnesses, not PR count or tokens burned.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Rewards should be centered around producing value. elegant, well-factored, pragmatic system design and around clarity of test and evaluation harnesses.

takeaways.technique: Adversarial checks and explicit definitions of done baked into workflow
takeaways.what_they_do: Bake planning, review, adversarial checks, and context management into the orchestration workflow rather than relying on ad-hoc human process.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The planning, the review, the adversarial checks, the context management.
